title: How to run openvino on a single thread?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
`ov::inference_num_threads` limits the number of logical processors used for CPU inference.

`compiled_model = core.compile_model(model, device_name, ov::inference_num_threads(1));`

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1  I have tried above mentioned solution but it still takes multiple threads.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
In that case, you have to build open source OpenVINO with -DTHREADING=SEQ to disable threading optimizations.

Ref: [17566](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/issues/17566)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1  Let me try this then I will update.

comments.author: participant2
participant3
reporter
comments.body: @participant1  My use case is to only create one thread and run inference on this thread.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter Since OpenVINO supports both synchronous inference and asynchronous inference, OpenVINO will create additional thread for asynchronous inference during compiling model even if `ov::inference_num_threads(1)`. Then if user use `infer_request.infer()` to trigger synchronous inference, inference will run on original thread.

So application creates two threads and only runs one. May I know if it is acceptable in your use case? 

If yes, please try below steps:

1. Build OpenVINO with `-DTHREADING=SEQ` 
2. Compile model with `ov::inference_num_threads(1)`
3. Use `infer_request.infer()` to trigger synchronous inference
